title.zh: 卷五 本紀第五 成祖一
title.raw: 卷五 本紀第五 成祖一 Volume 5 Annals 5: Chengzu 1

sentences.zh: 成祖啟天弘道高明肇運聖武神功純仁至孝文皇帝諱棣，太祖第四子也。

translations.literal: Chengzu, Emperor Wen, styled Opener of Heaven, Broadener of the Way, Lofty and Bright, Founder of the Fortune, Sacred in Martial Valor and Divine in Achievement, Pure in Benevolence and Supreme in Filial Piety — taboo name Di — was the fourth son of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu, the Emperor Wen, whose posthumous titles ran through Opener of Heaven, Broadener of the Way, Lofty and Bright, Founder of the Fortune, Sacred in Martial Valor and Divine in Achievement, Pure in Benevolence and Supreme in Filial Piety, bore the personal name Di and was the fourth son of the dynastic founder.

sentences.zh: 母孝慈高皇后。

translations.literal: His mother was the Empress Xiaoci Gao.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Empress Ma, posthumously honored as the Xiaoci Gao Empress.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年，封燕王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year 3 he received the title Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 十三年，之籓北平。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he went to his fief at Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 he took up residence in his apanage at Beiping.

sentences.zh: 王貌奇偉，美髭髯。

translations.literal: The Prince's appearance was singularly imposing; his beard and mustache were handsome.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince was striking in stature, with a fine beard and mustache.

sentences.zh: 智勇有大略，能推誠任人。

translations.literal: Wise and brave, possessed of great strategic vision, he could employ men by extending sincere trust.
translations.idiomatic: He combined wisdom and courage with far-reaching design, and won service by treating men with open sincerity.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，同晉王討鼐爾不哈。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, together with the Prince of Jin he campaigned against Nayir Buqa.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 he joined the Prince of Jin in a campaign against Nayir Buqa.

sentences.zh: 晉王怯不敢進，王倍道趨伊都山，獲其全部而還，太祖大喜，是後屢帥諸將出征，並令王節制沿邊士馬，王威名大振。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin was timid and dared not advance; the Prince doubled his march to Yidu Mountain, took the entire enemy force, and returned. Taizu was greatly pleased. Thereafter he repeatedly led the generals on campaign and was also ordered to command the border troops and horses along the frontier. The Prince's renown greatly increased.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Jin hung back in fear, but the Prince of Yan forced the march to Mount Yidu, captured the whole enemy host, and returned in triumph. Taizu was delighted. After that he often led the generals in the field and was given authority over frontier soldiers and horses; his name resounded along the border.

sentences.zh: 秋七月癸酉，匿壮士端禮門，紿貴、昺入，殺之，遂奪九門。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, on the day guiyou, he hid stalwart men at the Gate of Courteous Rites, lured Gui and Bing inside, killed them, and seized the Nine Gates.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou in the seventh month he concealed picked warriors at the Gate of Courteous Rites, drew in Zhang Bing and Xie Gui, killed them, and took the Nine Gates.

sentences.zh: 上書天子，指泰、子澄為奸臣，並援《祖訓》「朝無正臣，内有奸惡，則親王訓兵待命，天子密詔諸王統領鎮兵討平之」。

translations.literal: He sent up a memorial to the Son of Heaven, denouncing Tai and Zicheng as treacherous ministers, and citing the Ancestral Instructions: "When the court lacks upright ministers and evil men arise within, the imperial princes shall drill their troops and await orders; the Son of Heaven will secretly instruct the princes to lead the garrison forces and suppress them."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne, naming Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng as traitors and invoking the Ancestral Instructions: when the court has no upright ministers and villains stir within, imperial princes are to ready their troops and await command, and the Son of Heaven will secretly order the princes to lead frontier forces and put the rebellion down.

sentences.zh: 書既發，遂舉兵。

translations.literal: Once the memorial had been sent, he raised his army.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial dispatched, he took up arms.

sentences.zh: 自署官屬，號其師曰「靖難」。

translations.literal: He appointed his own officials and styled his army the "Pacification of Difficulties."
translations.idiomatic: He set up his own staff and called his host the Army of Pacifying the Realm's Troubles.

sentences.zh: 拔居庸關，破懷來，執宋忠，取密雲，克遵化，降永平。

translations.literal: He took Juyong Pass, broke Huailai, seized Song Zhong, captured Miyun, took Zunhua, and received the surrender of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: He carried Juyong Pass, stormed Huailai, took Song Zhong prisoner, seized Miyun, captured Zunhua, and won Yongping over.

sentences.zh: 二旬，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: Within twenty days his forces reached several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In twenty days his following swelled to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 八月，天子以耿炳文為大將軍，帥師致討。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Son of Heaven appointed Geng Bingwen grand general and sent him to campaign against the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the court named Geng Bingwen grand general and marched him against the Prince.

sentences.zh: 己酉，師至真定，前鋒抵雄縣。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou the army reached Zhending; the vanguard reached Xiong County.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou the main force reached Zhending while the van pressed to Xiong County.

sentences.zh: 壬子，王夜渡白溝河，圍雄，拔其城，屠之。

translations.literal: On the day renzi the Prince crossed the Baigou River by night, besieged Xiong, took the city, and put it to the sword.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi the Prince forded the Baigou by night, invested Xiong, stormed it, and slaughtered the garrison.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，都指揮潘忠、楊松自鄚州來援，伏兵擒之，遂据鄚州，還駐白溝。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin the commanders-in-chief Pan Zhong and Yang Song came from Mozhou to relieve the city; ambush troops seized them, and the Prince then held Mozhou and returned to camp on the Baigou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the commanders Pan Zhong and Yang Song marched from Mozhou to the rescue; the Prince's ambush took them, and he seized Mozhou before withdrawing to the Baigou.

sentences.zh: 大將軍部校張保來降，言大將軍軍三十萬，先至者十三萬，半營滹沱河南，半營河北。

translations.literal: Zhang Bao, a junior officer of the grand general, came over and reported that the grand general's army numbered three hundred thousand, of whom one hundred thirty thousand had arrived first — half encamped south of the Hutuo River and half north of it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bao, a staff officer under Geng Bingwen, defected and said the grand general had three hundred thousand men, with one hundred thirty thousand already up — half south of the Hutuo and half on the north bank.

sentences.zh: 王懼與北軍戰，南軍且乘之也，乃縱保歸，俾揚言王帥兵且至，誘其軍盡北渡河。

translations.literal: The Prince feared fighting the northern army while the southern army might take advantage; he therefore released Bao to return and had him spread word that the Prince's main force was about to arrive, luring the enemy to cross the river entirely to the north.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a clash with the northern wing while the southerners exploited his flank, the Prince sent Bao back with a story that the Prince's main body was closing in, drawing the whole enemy host across to the north bank.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，王至真定，與張玉、譚淵等夾擊炳文軍，大破之，獲其副將李堅、甯忠及都督顧成等，斬首三萬級。

translations.literal: On the day renxu the Prince reached Zhending; with Zhang Yu, Tan Yuan, and others he attacked Bingwen's army from both sides, routed it utterly, and captured his lieutenant generals Li Jian and Ning Zhong and the regional commander Gu Cheng; heads taken numbered thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu he came to Zhending and, with Zhang Yu and Tan Yuan, caught Geng Bingwen in a pincer, broke him completely, and took his deputies Li Jian and Ning Zhong and the regional commander Gu Cheng; thirty thousand heads were counted.

sentences.zh: 進圍真定，二日不下，乃引去。

translations.literal: He pressed the siege of Zhending; after two days it did not fall, and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He invested Zhending for two days without success, then drew off.

sentences.zh: 天子聞炳文敗，遣曹國公李景隆代領其軍。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven heard of Bingwen's defeat, he sent the Duke of Cao, Li Jinglong, to replace him in command of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Geng Bingwen's rout, the court sent the Duke of Cao, Li Jinglong, to take over the army.

sentences.zh: 九月戊辰，江陰侯吳高以遼東兵圍永平。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the day wuchen, the Marquis of Jiangyin, Wu Gao, invested Yongping with Liaodong troops.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen in the ninth month the Marquis of Jiangyin, Wu Gao, laid siege to Yongping with troops from Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，景隆合兵五十萬，進營河間。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin Jinglong united five hundred thousand men and advanced to encamp at Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Li Jinglong massed five hundred thousand men and moved to camp at Hejian.

sentences.zh: 王語諸將曰：「景隆色厲而中餒，聞我在必不敢遽來，不若往援永平以致其師。

translations.literal: The Prince told his generals: "Jinglong looks fierce but is hollow within. Hearing that I am here he will not dare come at once. Better to go relieve Yongping and draw him out.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince told his commanders, "Jinglong blusters but his heart fails him. While he knows I am here he will not rush forward — we should relieve Yongping and pull him after us.

sentences.zh: 吳高怯不任戰，我至必走，然後還擊景隆。

translations.literal: Wu Gao is timid and unfit for battle; when I arrive he is sure to flee; then we can turn and strike Jinglong.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Gao is a coward and no fighter; once I appear he will run, and then we can wheel back on Jinglong.

sentences.zh: 堅城在前，大軍在后，必成擒矣。

translations.literal: With a strong city before him and a great army behind, he is sure to be taken."
translations.idiomatic: A walled city in front and a great host behind — he will be ours."

sentences.zh: 」丙戌，燕師援永平。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu the Yan army marched to relieve Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the Yan host set out for Yongping.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，吳高聞王至，果走，追擊敗之。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, when Wu Gao heard the Prince had come, he indeed fled; the Prince pursued and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Wu Gao, hearing the Prince was near, fled as foretold; the Prince chased him down and broke his force.

sentences.zh: 遂北趨大宁。

translations.literal: He then pressed north toward Da Ning.
translations.idiomatic: He then drove north toward Da Ning.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以計入其城。

translations.literal: On the day renyin he entered the city by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin he gained the city by ruse.

sentences.zh: 居七日，挾寧王權，拔大寧之眾及朶顏三衛卒俱南。

translations.literal: After seven days he compelled the Prince of Ning, Quan, took the troops of Da Ning and the soldiers of the three guards of the Tumed, and all marched south together.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days on he coerced the Prince of Ning, Quan, and marched south with the Da Ning host and the warriors of the three Tumed guards.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，至會州，始立五軍。

translations.literal: On the day yimao he reached Huizhou and for the first time established the Five Armies.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao he reached Huizhou and first organized the Five Armies.

sentences.zh: 張玉將中軍，郑亨、何寿副之；

translations.literal: Zhang Yu commanded the center army, with Zheng Heng and He Shou as his deputies;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yu led the center, with Zheng Heng and He Shou as deputies;

sentences.zh: 朱能將左軍，朱榮、李浚副之；

translations.literal: Zhu Neng commanded the left army, with Zhu Rong and Li Jun as his deputies;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Neng led the left, with Zhu Rong and Li Jun as deputies;

sentences.zh: 李彬將右軍，徐理、孟善副之；

translations.literal: Li Bin commanded the right army, with Xu Li and Meng Shan as his deputies;
translations.idiomatic: Li Bin led the right, with Xu Li and Meng Shan as deputies;

sentences.zh: 徐忠將前軍，陳文、吳達副之；

translations.literal: Xu Zhong commanded the forward army, with Chen Wen and Wu Da as his deputies;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhong led the van, with Chen Wen and Wu Da as deputies;

sentences.zh: 房寬將后軍，和允中、毛整副之。

translations.literal: Fang Kuan commanded the rear army, with He Yunzhong and Mao Zheng as his deputies.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Kuan led the rear, with He Yunzhong and Mao Zheng as deputies.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，入松亭關。

translations.literal: On the day dingsi he entered Songting Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi he passed through Songting Pass.

sentences.zh: 景隆聞王征大宁，果引軍圍北平，筑垒九門，世子堅守不戰。

translations.literal: When Jinglong heard the Prince had gone to Da Ning, he indeed led his army to besiege Beiping, built ramparts at the Nine Gates, and the heir apparent held firm without giving battle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinglong, learning the Prince had gone to Da Ning, did invest Beiping, threw up works at the Nine Gates, and the heir apparent held the walls without fighting.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚午，王次孤山。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day gengwu, the Prince halted at Gushan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on gengwu, the Prince made camp at Gushan.

sentences.zh: 逻骑還报曰白河流澌不可渡。

translations.literal: Scouts returned and reported that the Bai River's ice was breaking up and could not be crossed.
translations.idiomatic: Patrols came back saying the ice on the Bai River was breaking and the crossing was impossible.

sentences.zh: 王祷於神，至則冰合，乃济師。

translations.literal: The Prince prayed to the spirits; when he arrived the ice had joined solid, and he crossed his army.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince prayed; when he reached the river the floes had knit into a road, and he took his army across.

sentences.zh: 景隆遣都督陳晖侦敌，道左，出王軍后。

translations.literal: Jinglong sent the regional commander Chen Hui to reconnoiter the enemy; he took the left road and came out behind the Prince's army.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinglong sent the regional commander Chen Hui to scout; Chen took the left track and fell in behind the Prince's line.

sentences.zh: 王分軍還擊之，晖眾爭渡河，冰忽解，溺死無算。

translations.literal: The Prince divided his force to strike back; Hui's men scrambled to cross the river, the ice suddenly broke apart, and countless drowned.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince split off a detachment to hit him from behind; Chen Hui's men rushed the river, the ice gave way, and the drowned were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 辛未，與景隆戰於郑村坝。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei he fought Jinglong at Zhengcun Dam.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei he met Li Jinglong at Zhengcun Dam.

sentences.zh: 王以精骑先破其七營，諸將继至，景隆大敗，奔還。

translations.literal: The Prince with picked cavalry first broke seven of his camps; the other generals followed, Jinglong was utterly defeated and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: With elite horsemen he shattered seven camps in succession; the other commanders piled on, Li Jinglong was routed, and fled.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，复上書自诉。

translations.literal: On the day yihai he again sent up a memorial pleading his own case.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai he again memorialized the throne in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 十二月，景隆调兵德州，期以明年春大舉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Jinglong redeployed his troops at Dezhou, planning a great advance in the coming spring.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Li Jinglong regrouped at Dezhou, intending a major campaign the next spring.

sentences.zh: 王乃謀侵大同，曰：「攻大同，彼必赴救，大同苦寒，南軍脆弱，且不戰疲矣。

translations.literal: The Prince then planned to strike Datong, saying: "If we attack Datong they are sure to hurry to its relief. Datong is bitterly cold; the southern troops are frail, and they will be worn down without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince turned toward Datong, saying, "Strike Datong and they must march to save it — a land of killing cold where southern soldiers wilt before they even fight."

sentences.zh: 」庚申，降广昌。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen he received the surrender of Guangchang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Guangchang submitted.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月丙寅，克蔚州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year, on the day bingyin, he took Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of year 2, on bingyin in the first month, he captured Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 二月癸丑，至大同。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day guichou, he reached Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guichou, he arrived at Datong.

sentences.zh: 景隆果由紫荆關來援。

translations.literal: Jinglong indeed came by the Zijing Pass to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinglong, as expected, came through Zijing Pass to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 王已旋軍居庸，景隆兵多冻餒死者，不见敌而還。

translations.literal: The Prince had already wheeled his army back to Juyong; many of Jinglong's troops died of cold and hunger, and seeing no enemy he returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince had already swung back to Juyong; Li Jinglong's men froze and starved by the thousands, found no foe, and trudged home.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，景隆進兵河間，與郭英、吳杰、平安期會白溝河。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer Jinglong advanced on Hejian; he and Guo Ying, Wu Jie, and Ping An arranged to meet at the Baigou River.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Li Jinglong pushed on Hejian and arranged with Guo Ying, Wu Jie, and Ping An to join at the Baigou.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，王營苏家桥。

translations.literal: On the day yimao the Prince encamped at Sujia Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the Prince camped at Sujia Bridge.

sentences.zh: 己未，遇平安兵河侧。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei he encountered Ping An's troops on the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei he ran into Ping An's force on the river flats.

sentences.zh: 王以百骑前，佯卻，誘安阵动，乘之，安敗走。

translations.literal: The Prince rode forward with a hundred horsemen, feigned retreat, lured An's formation into movement, and struck when it did; An was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince led a hundred riders forward, pretended to flee, drew Ping An's line into disorder, and charged; Ping An broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 遂薄景隆軍，戰不利。

translations.literal: He then pressed close on Jinglong's army; the battle went ill.
translations.idiomatic: He closed on Li Jinglong's host, but the fight turned against him.

sentences.zh: 暝收軍，王以三骑殿，夜迷失道，下馬伏地视河流，乃辨東西，渡河去。

translations.literal: At dusk he gathered his troops; the Prince with three horsemen brought up the rear. By night he lost the road, dismounted, lay on the ground to watch the stream, and so distinguished east from west, crossed the river, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he drew in his men; the Prince himself rearguarded with three riders. Night found him off the track; he dismounted, pressed his ear to the water to read its flow, found east from west, forded, and escaped.

sentences.zh: 庚申，复戰。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen he fought again.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen battle was joined again.

sentences.zh: 景隆横阵數十里，破燕后軍。

translations.literal: Jinglong drew up his line for tens of li and broke the Yan rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinglong's battle line stretched for tens of li and shattered the Yan rear.

sentences.zh: 王自帥精骑横擊之，斬瞿能父子。

translations.literal: The Prince himself led picked cavalry in a lateral strike and cut down Qu Neng, father and son.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince led picked cavalry in a flanking blow and killed Qu Neng and his son.

sentences.zh: 令丘福冲中堅，不得入。

translations.literal: He ordered Qiu Fu to pierce the center but he could not break through.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Qiu Fu to punch the center, but Qiu Fu could not break in.

sentences.zh: 王荡其左，景隆兵乃绕出王后，大戰良久，飞矢雨注。

translations.literal: The Prince swept their left; Jinglong's troops then wheeled out behind the Prince's rear, and a great battle lasted long while arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince rolled up their left; Li Jinglong's men curled behind him, and the fight dragged on under a rain of arrows.

sentences.zh: 王三易馬，矢盡揮剑，剑折走登堤，佯引鞭若招后继者。

translations.literal: The Prince changed horses three times; when his arrows were spent he swung his sword; the blade broke and he ran up an embankment, feigning to raise his whip as though summoning followers behind.
translations.idiomatic: Three horses fell under him; when his quiver was empty he hacked with his sword until the blade snapped; he scrambled onto a dike and flicked his whip as if calling up reserves.

sentences.zh: 景隆疑有伏，不敢前，高煦救至，乃解。

translations.literal: Jinglong suspected an ambush and dared not advance; Gaoxu came to the rescue, and the danger passed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jinglong feared a trap and held back; Zhu Gaoxu arrived in time and the Prince was saved.

sentences.zh: 時南軍益集，燕將士皆失色。

translations.literal: At that time the southern army was gathering ever thicker; the Yan officers and soldiers all turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: More southern troops poured in by the hour, and the Yan ranks went grey with fear.

sentences.zh: 王奋然曰：「吾不進，敌不退，有戰耳。

translations.literal: The Prince said with spirit: "If I do not advance, the enemy will not retreat — there is nothing but to fight."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince roused them: "Stand still and they will not leave — there is only to fight."

sentences.zh: 」乃复以劲卒突出其背，夾攻之。

translations.literal: He then again sent crack troops to burst out behind them and attacked from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: He threw fresh shock troops through their rear and closed from both sides.

sentences.zh: 會旋风起，折景隆旗，王乘风縱火奋擊，斬首數萬溺死者十余萬人。

translations.literal: A whirlwind arose, snapping Jinglong's banners; the Prince rode the wind, set fires, and struck fiercely; heads taken numbered in the tens of thousands, and those drowned exceeded one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: A whirlwind snapped Li Jinglong's standards; the Prince rode the gust, fired the field, and cut deep — tens of thousands slain and more than a hundred thousand drowned.

sentences.zh: 郭英溃而西，景隆溃而南，盡丧其所賜玺書斧钺，走德州。

translations.literal: Guo Ying broke west; Jinglong broke south; they lost entirely the imperial seals, writs, axes, and halberds they had been granted, and fled to Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ying fled west, Li Jinglong south, abandoning the seals, commissions, axes, and halberds the throne had bestowed, and ran for Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 五月癸酉，王入德州，景隆走济南。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day guiyou, the Prince entered Dezhou; Jinglong fled to Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guiyou, the Prince entered Dezhou; Li Jinglong escaped to Jinan.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，攻济南，敗景隆軍城下。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen he attacked Jinan and defeated Jinglong's army below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen he assaulted Jinan and broke Li Jinglong's force beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 铁铉、盛庸堅守，不克。

translations.literal: Tie Xuan and Sheng Yong held firm; the city could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Tie Xuan and Sheng Yong held fast, and the city would not fall.

sentences.zh: 秋八月戊申，解圍還北平。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day wushen, he raised the siege and returned to Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wushen, he lifted the siege and returned to Beiping.

sentences.zh: 九月，盛庸代李景隆將，复取德州，與吳杰、平安、徐凯相掎角，以困北平。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Sheng Yong replaced Li Jinglong in command, retook Dezhou, and with Wu Jie, Ping An, and Xu Kai formed a pincer to hem in Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Sheng Yong took command from Li Jinglong, recovered Dezhou, and with Wu Jie, Ping An, and Xu Kai set a pincer meant to choke Beiping.

sentences.zh: 時徐凯方城沧州，王佯出兵攻遼東，至通州，循河而南，渡直沽，昼夜兼行。

translations.literal: At that time Xu Kai was investing Cangzhou; the Prince feigned a march on Liaodong, reached Tongzhou, followed the river south, crossed Zhigu, and marched day and night without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Kai was then besieging Cangzhou; the Prince pretended a strike into Liaodong, reached Tongzhou, turned south along the canal, crossed Zhigu, and drove without pause day or night.

sentences.zh: 冬十月戊午，襲執徐凯，破其城，夜坑降卒三千人。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the day wuwu, he surprised and seized Xu Kai, broke his city, and that night buried alive three thousand surrendered soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu in the tenth month he sprang on Xu Kai, stormed Cangzhou, and that night buried three thousand captives alive.

sentences.zh: 遂渡河过德州。

translations.literal: He then crossed the river and passed Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He forded on and passed Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 盛庸遣兵來襲，擊敗之。

translations.literal: Sheng Yong sent troops to strike him; he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong sent a column against him; the Prince beat it off.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬申，至臨清。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day renshen, he reached Linqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renshen, he reached Linqing.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁酉，襲破盛庸將孫霖於滑口。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the day dingyou, he surprised and broke Sheng Yong's general Sun Lin at Huakou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingyou, he surprised Sheng Yong's general Sun Lin at Huakou and shattered him.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，及庸戰於東昌，庸以火器劲弩歼王兵。

translations.literal: On the day yimao he fought Yong at Dongchang; Yong with fire weapons and powerful crossbows annihilated the Prince's troops.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao he met Sheng Yong at Dongchang; fire weapons and heavy crossbows cut the Prince's men to pieces.

sentences.zh: 會平安軍至，合圍數重，王大敗，溃圍以免，亡數萬人，張玉戰死。

translations.literal: Ping An's army arrived; they surrounded him in many rings; the Prince was utterly defeated, broke out of the encirclement and escaped, losing tens of thousands; Zhang Yu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An came up and ringed him in layer after layer; the Prince suffered a crushing defeat, hacked his way out, left tens of thousands dead on the field, and Zhang Yu fell fighting.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月辛酉，敗吳杰、平安於威縣，又敗之於深州，遂還北平。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, on the day xinyou, he defeated Wu Jie and Ping An at Wei County and again at Shenzhou, then returned to Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year 3, on xinyou, he routed Wu Jie and Ping An at Wei County and again at Shenzhou, then withdrew to Beiping.

sentences.zh: 二月乙巳，复帥師南下。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the day yisi, he again led his army south.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on yisi, he marched south once more.

sentences.zh: 三月辛巳，與盛庸遇於夾河，譚淵戰死。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day xinsi, he met Sheng Yong at Jiahe; Tan Yuan died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinsi, he clashed with Sheng Yong at Jiahe; Tan Yuan was killed.

sentences.zh: 朱能、張武殊死斗，庸軍少卻。

translations.literal: Zhu Neng and Zhang Wu fought to the death; Yong's army fell back slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Neng and Zhang Wu fought as if each man were the last; Sheng Yong's line bent back a little.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，各敛兵入營。

translations.literal: At dusk each side gathered its troops into camp.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk both sides drew into camp.

sentences.zh: 王以十余骑逼庸營野宿，及明起视，已在圍中。

translations.literal: The Prince with a little more than ten horsemen pressed close to Yong's camp and slept in the open; when dawn came he looked about and found himself already within the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince camped with barely a dozen riders under Sheng Yong's very sentries; at dawn he woke surrounded.

sentences.zh: 乃从容引馬，鸣角穿營而去。

translations.literal: He then calmly led his horse, sounded the horn, and rode through the camp and out.
translations.idiomatic: He simply walked his mount, blew his horn, and rode through the enemy lines and away.

sentences.zh: 諸將以天子有詔，毋使负殺叔父名，仓卒相顧愕貽，不敢发一矢。

translations.literal: The generals, because the Son of Heaven had an edict that they must not earn the name of killing their uncle, stared at one another in alarm and hesitation and dared not loose a single arrow.
translations.idiomatic: The southern commanders, bound by the Son of Heaven's order not to bear the guilt of slaying their uncle, gaped at one another and would not draw a bow.

sentences.zh: 是日复戰，自辰至未，两軍相胜负，東北风忽起，尘埃蔽天，燕兵大呼，乘风縱擊，庸大敗。

translations.literal: That day they fought again; from the hour chen to the hour wei the two armies traded victories; a northeast wind suddenly rose, dust blotted out the sky, the Yan troops shouted, and riding the wind they struck with fire; Yong was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They fought again from chen to wei with neither side gaining; then a northeast gale blew up, dust swallowed the field, the Yan men roared, and charging with flame they broke Sheng Yong completely.

sentences.zh: 走德州。

translations.literal: He fled to Dezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yong fled to Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 吳杰、平安自真定引軍與庸會，未至八十里，聞敗引還。

translations.literal: Wu Jie and Ping An led their armies from Zhending to join Yong; before they had gone eighty li they heard of the defeat and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jie and Ping An marched from Zhending to meet Sheng Yong; eighty li short of him they heard of the rout and turned back.

sentences.zh: 王以計誘之，杰、安出兵襲王。

translations.literal: The Prince lured them by stratagem; Jie and An led their troops out to surprise the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince baited them; Wu Jie and Ping An sallied to ambush him.

sentences.zh: 闰月戊戌，遇於藁城。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the day wuxu, they met at Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on wuxu, the armies met at Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 己亥，與戰，大风拔木，杰、安敗走，追至真定城下。

translations.literal: On the jihai day, they fought; a great wind uprooted trees; Jie and An were defeated and fled; the pursuit reached below the walls of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai they gave battle. A gale tore trees from the earth; Wu Jie and Ping An broke and ran, pursued to the foot of Zhending’s walls.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，至大名，聞齊泰、黄子澄已罢，上書请召還吳杰、平安、盛庸兵。

translations.literal: On the guichou day, he reached Daming; hearing that Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng had already been dismissed, he submitted a memorial asking that the armies of Wu Jie, Ping An, and Sheng Yong be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou he came to Daming. Learning that Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng had been removed from office, he memorialized the throne to recall the forces of Wu Jie, Ping An, and Sheng Yong.

sentences.zh: 天子使大理少卿薛岩來报，谕王释甲，王不奉詔。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent Xue Yan, Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, to report; he instructed the Prince to lay down arms; the Prince did not obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Xue Yan, vice minister of the Court of Judicial Review, with a reply urging the prince to disarm. The prince refused the command.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，杰、安、庸分兵斷燕饷道，王遣指揮武胜上書，诘其故。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer, Jie, An, and Yong divided their forces to cut the Yan supply route; the Prince sent the commander Wu Sheng to submit a memorial questioning the reason.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, in the fifth month, Jie, An, and Yong split their armies to sever the Yan supply lines. The prince sent Commander Wu Sheng to demand an explanation in writing.

sentences.zh: 天子怒，下胜狱。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was angry and imprisoned Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and threw Sheng into prison.

sentences.zh: 王遂遣李远略沛縣，焚粮舟萬計。

translations.literal: The Prince then sent Li Yuan to raid Pei County and burned grain boats by the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The prince then dispatched Li Yuan against Pei County and burned grain barges by the ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 秋七月己丑，掠彰德。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn, on the jichou day, he plundered Zhangde.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn’s seventh month, on jichou, he ravaged Zhangde.

sentences.zh: 丙申，降林縣。

translations.literal: On the bingshen day, Lin County submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Lin County surrendered.

sentences.zh: 平安乘虚捣北平，王遣劉江迎戰，安敗走。

translations.literal: Ping An, seizing an opening, struck at Beiping; the Prince sent Liu Jiang to meet him in battle; An was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An stole a march on Beiping while the prince’s main force was away. The prince sent Liu Jiang to meet him; An was beaten and fled.

sentences.zh: 房昭屯易州西水寨，攻保定，王引兵圍之。

translations.literal: Fang Zhao encamped at the West Water Stockade in Yizhou and attacked Baoding; the Prince led troops to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zhao held the West Water Stockade near Yizhou and pressed Baoding. The prince marched to encircle him.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁巳，都指揮花英援昭，敗之峨眉山下，斬首萬級，昭弃寨走。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the dingsi day, Chief Commander Hua Ying came to relieve Zhao; he was defeated below Emei Mountain; heads cut numbered in the ten thousands; Zhao abandoned the stockade and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In winter’s tenth month, on dingsi, Chief Commander Hua Ying marched to relieve Zhao. Below Emei Mountain he was shattered; ten thousand heads were taken. Zhao abandoned the camp and ran.

sentences.zh: 己卯，還北平。

translations.literal: On the jimao day, he returned to Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao he returned to Beiping.

sentences.zh: 十一月乙巳，王自為文祭南北阵亡將士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the yisi day, the Prince himself composed a text to sacrifice to the officers and soldiers who had fallen on the northern and southern sides.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on yisi, the prince himself drafted a ritual address and sacrificed to the dead of both armies, north and south.

sentences.zh: 当是時，王稱兵三年矣。

translations.literal: At that time, the Prince had raised arms for three years.
translations.idiomatic: By then the prince had been at war for three years.

sentences.zh: 親戰阵，冒矢石，以身先士卒，常乘胜逐北，然亦屢濒於危。

translations.literal: He personally fought in the ranks, braved arrows and stones, took the lead before his soldiers, often rode victory in pursuit of a fleeing foe, yet also repeatedly came to the brink of peril.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in the front line himself, under arrow and stone, always ahead of his men, often chasing a broken enemy—but again and again he brushed death.

sentences.zh: 所克城邑，兵去旋复為朝廷守，仅据有北平、保定、永平三府而已。

translations.literal: Of the cities he took, once his troops departed they were soon held again for the court; he held only the three prefectures of Beiping, Baoding, and Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Cities he seized slipped back to the court the moment his columns moved on. He truly held only Beiping, Baoding, and Yongping.

sentences.zh: 無何，中官被黜者來奔，具言京師空虚可取状。

translations.literal: Before long, a eunuch who had been dismissed came to defect and fully described how the capital was empty and could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a cashiered palace eunuch fled to him and described the capital in detail—how hollow it was, how ripe for the taking.

sentences.zh: 王乃慨然曰：「频年用兵，何時已平？

translations.literal: The Prince then said with emotion: “Years on end we have waged war—when will it ever be settled?
translations.idiomatic: The prince spoke with sudden passion: “Year after year we have fought. When will this ever end?

sentences.zh: 要当臨江一决，不复返顧矣。

translations.literal: We must settle it in one decision on the river; we shall not turn back again.
translations.idiomatic: We must stake everything on one crossing of the Yangtze. I will not look back again.”

sentences.zh: 」十二月丙寅，复出師。

translations.literal: ” In the twelfth month, on the bingyin day, he marched out again.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on bingyin, he took the field once more.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月乙未，由馆陶渡河。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the fourth year, on the yiwei day, he crossed the river from Guantao.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the fourth year, on yiwei in the first month, he forded the river at Guantao.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，徇徐州。

translations.literal: On the guichou day, he swept through Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou he overran Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月壬辰，平安以四萬骑蹑王軍，王設伏淝河，大敗之。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the renchen day, Ping An with forty thousand horsemen followed on the Prince’s army; the Prince set an ambush at the Fei River and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on renchen, Ping An came after him with forty thousand horse. The prince laid an ambush on the Fei River and broke them utterly.

sentences.zh: 丙午，遣譚清斷徐州饷道，還至大店，為铁铉軍所圍。

translations.literal: On the bingwu day, he sent Tan Qing to cut the Xuzhou supply route; returning to Dadian, he was surrounded by Tie Xuan’s army.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu he sent Tan Qing to sever Xuzhou’s supply line. Tan returned as far as Dadian and there was trapped by Tie Xuan’s force.

sentences.zh: 王引兵驰援，清突圍出，合擊敗之。

translations.literal: The Prince led troops in urgent relief; Qing broke out of the encirclement; they joined in attack and defeated the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The prince rushed to his rescue. Qing burst the ring; together they struck and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙寅，王營小河，為桥以济，平安趨爭桥，陳文戰死。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on the bingyin day, the Prince encamped at Xiaohe, built a bridge to cross, Ping An rushed to contest the bridge, and Chen Wen died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, in the fourth month on bingyin, the prince camped at Xiaohe and threw a bridge across. Ping An raced to seize it; Chen Wen fell fighting.

sentences.zh: 平安軍桥南，王軍桥北，相持數日。

translations.literal: Ping An’s army was south of the bridge, the Prince’s army north of the bridge; they faced each other for several days.
translations.idiomatic: An held the south bank, the prince the north. For days neither side yielded.

sentences.zh: 平安转戰，遇王於北坂，王几為安槊所及。

translations.literal: Ping An shifted to battle; he met the Prince at North Slope; the Prince was nearly reached by An’s spear.
translations.idiomatic: Ping An wheeled to fight again and met the prince on North Slope. An’s spear nearly found him.

sentences.zh: 番骑王骐跃入阵，掖王逸去。

translations.literal: The barbarian horseman Wang Qi leaped into the formation and, supporting the Prince, bore him away to safety.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier rider Wang Qi plunged into the press, caught the prince under his arm, and dragged him clear.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「南軍饥，更一二日饷至，猝未易破。

translations.literal: The Prince said: “The southern army is hungry; in another day or two their supplies will arrive; suddenly they will not be easy to break.
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, “The southern army is starving. In a day or two their grain will come up. Then they will not break easily.

sentences.zh: 」乃令千余人守桥，夜半渡河而南，绕出安軍后。

translations.literal: ” He then ordered a little more than a thousand men to hold the bridge; at midnight he crossed the river to the south and circled behind An’s army.
translations.idiomatic: He left a thousand men on the bridge, crossed by night to the south bank, and swung behind Ping An’s rear.

sentences.zh: 比旦，安始觉，适徐辉祖來會。

translations.literal: By dawn An first realized it; just then Xu Huizu came to join him.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn An realized what had happened—just as Xu Huizu arrived to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，大戰齊眉山下。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day, a great battle was fought below Qimei Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu they fought a great battle below Qimei Mountain.

sentences.zh: 時燕连失大將，淮士盛暑蒸湿，諸將请休軍小河東，就麦观衅。

translations.literal: At that time Yan had lost great generals in succession; the Huai region’s soil in the height of summer was steamy and wet; the commanders asked to rest the army east of Xiaohe and watch the wheat fields for an opening.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had lately lost one great commander after another. The Huai country sweltered in midsummer damp; the generals begged to halt east of Xiaohe, rest among the wheat, and wait for a chance.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「今敌持久饥疲，遮其饷道，可以坐困，奈何北渡懈將士心。

translations.literal: The Prince said: “Now the enemy has long been hungry and weary; block their supply route and they can be worn down sitting still—why cross north and slacken the soldiers’ hearts?
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, “The foe has been hungry and exhausted for weeks. Cut their supplies and we can crush them without stirring—why recross the river and loosen our men’s grip?

sentences.zh: 」乃下令欲渡河者左，諸將爭趨左。

translations.literal: ” He then ordered that whoever wished to cross the river should go to the left; the commanders all rushed to the left.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every man who wanted to retreat to stand on the left. The generals stampeded left.

sentences.zh: 王怒曰：「任公等所之。

translations.literal: The Prince said in anger: “Go where you will.
translations.idiomatic: The prince snapped, “Go, then—wherever you please.

sentences.zh: 」乃無敢复言。

translations.literal: ” Then none dared speak again.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared speak again.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，何福等營灵璧，燕遮其饷道，平安分兵六萬人护之。

translations.literal: On the dingchou day, He Fu and others encamped at Lingbi; Yan blocked their supply route; Ping An divided sixty thousand men to escort provisions.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou He Fu camped at Lingbi. Yan interdicted his supplies; Ping An detached sixty thousand men to guard the convoys.

sentences.zh: 己卯，王帥精锐横擊。

translations.literal: On the jimao day, the Prince led picked troops in a lateral strike.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao the prince led his elite in a slashing charge across their line.

sentences.zh: 斷其軍為二。

translations.literal: He cut their army in two.
translations.idiomatic: He split their host in half.

sentences.zh: 何福空壁來援，王軍少卻，高煦伏兵起，福敗走。

translations.literal: He Fu came out with empty walls to rescue; the Prince’s army slightly withdrew; Gao Xu’s hidden troops rose; Fu was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He Fu stripped his camp to rescue the van. The prince’s line gave a little ground; Zhu Gaoxu’s ambush rose; Fu broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，進薄其垒，破之，生擒平安、陳晖等三十七人，何福走免。

translations.literal: On the xinsi day, he pressed close to their ramparts, broke them, took alive Ping An, Chen Hui, and thirty-seven others, and He Fu escaped.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi he closed on their fort, stormed it, and took Ping An, Chen Hui, and thirty-seven more alive. He Fu alone got away.

sentences.zh: 五月己丑，下泗州，謁祖陵，賜父老牛酒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the jichou day, he took Sizhou, visited the imperial tombs, and bestowed an old ox and wine on his father.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jichou, he seized Sizhou, paid homage at the ancestral tombs, and offered his father’s spirit an old ox and wine.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，盛庸扼淮南岸，朱能、丘福潛济襲走之，遂克盱貽。

translations.literal: On the xinmao day, Sheng Yong held the south bank of the Huai; Zhu Neng and Qiu Fu secretly crossed and struck; they routed him and then took Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Sheng Yong barred the south Huai. Zhu Neng and Qiu Fu forded in secret, swept him aside, and took Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，王集諸將議所向，或言宜取鳳阳，或言先取淮安。

translations.literal: On the guisi day, the Prince gathered the commanders to discuss where to turn; some said Fengyang should be taken, others said Huai’an should be taken first.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the prince called his captains to decide their next blow. Some urged Fengyang; others, Huai’an first.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「鳳阳楼橹完，淮安多积粟，攻之未易下。

translations.literal: The Prince said: “Fengyang’s towers and parapets are intact; Huai’an has much stored grain; neither will be easy to reduce.
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, “Fengyang’s walls are whole; Huai’an is fat with grain. Either will cost us dearly.

sentences.zh: 不若乘胜直趨揚州，指仪真，則淮、鳳自震。

translations.literal: Better to ride our victory straight at Yangzhou and point at Yizhen; then Huai and Feng will shake of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Better to drive while we are hot on Yangzhou and fix our aim on Yizhen. Huai and Feng will tremble without a siege.

sentences.zh: 我耀兵江上，京師孤危，必有内变。

translations.literal: When we display our arms on the river, the capital will stand alone in peril and there is sure to be turmoil within.
translations.idiomatic: Show our banners on the Yangtze and the capital will stand friendless. Turmoil inside is certain.”

sentences.zh: 」諸將皆曰善。

translations.literal: ” All the commanders said it was good.
translations.idiomatic: Every commander agreed.

sentences.zh: 己亥，徇揚州，駐軍江北。

translations.literal: On the jihai day, he swept Yangzhou and encamped his army north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he overran Yangzhou and pitched camp on the north bank.

sentences.zh: 天子遣慶成郡主至軍中，許割地以和，不听。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent the Princess of Qingcheng to the army, promising to cede territory for peace; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the Princess of Qingcheng to his camp with an offer of territory for peace. He would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 六月癸丑，江防都督佥事陳瑄以舟師叛，附於王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the guichou day, Chen Xuan, Assistant Commander-in-Chief of River Defense, rebelled with the fleet and attached himself to the Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on guichou, Chen Xuan, deputy commander of river defense, turned his fleet and joined the prince.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，祭大江。

translations.literal: On the jiayin day, he sacrificed to the Great River.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin he offered sacrifice to the Great River.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，自瓜州渡，盛庸以海艘迎戰，敗績。

translations.literal: On the yimao day, he crossed from Guazhou; Sheng Yong met him with sea-going vessels; he suffered a crushing defeat.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao he crossed from Guazhou. Sheng Yong met him with sea junks and was shattered.

sentences.zh: 戊午，下鎮江。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day, he took Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu he took Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 庚申，次龍潭。

translations.literal: On the gengshen day, he halted at Longtan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen he paused at Longtan.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，天子复遣大臣議割地，諸王继至，皆不听。

translations.literal: On the xinyou day, the Son of Heaven again sent great ministers to discuss ceding territory; princes arrived in succession; he would listen to none of them.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the emperor again sent high ministers to negotiate a cession of land. Imperial princes followed one after another. He listened to none.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，至金川門，谷王橞、李景隆等开門納王，都城遂陷。

translations.literal: On the yichou day, he reached Jinchuan Gate; the Prince of Gu Zhu Yunyi, Li Jinglong, and others opened the gate and admitted the Prince; the capital city then fell.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou he came to Jinchuan Gate. The Prince of Gu, Zhu Yunyi, Li Jinglong, and others opened the gates and let him in. The capital fell that day.

sentences.zh: 是日，王分命諸將守城及皇城，還駐龍江，下令抚安軍民。

translations.literal: That day, the Prince assigned the commanders in separate orders to guard the city and the imperial city; he returned to encamp at Longjiang and issued an order to pacify soldiers and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he posted his generals to hold the city and the Forbidden City, withdrew his headquarters to Longjiang, and proclaimed calm for soldiers and people alike.

sentences.zh: 大索齊泰、黄子澄、方孝孺等五十余人，榜其姓名曰奸臣。

translations.literal: He made a great search for Qi Tai, Huang Zicheng, Fang Xiaoru, and more than fifty others; he posted their names with the label “treacherous ministers.”
translations.idiomatic: He hunted Qi Tai, Huang Zicheng, Fang Xiaoru, and more than fifty besides, and posted their names under the heading “treacherous ministers.”

sentences.zh: 丙寅，諸王群臣上表勸進。

translations.literal: On the bingyin day, the princes and the civil and military officials submitted memorials urging him to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the princes and the court memorialized him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 己巳，王謁孝陵。

translations.literal: On the jisi day, the Prince visited the Xiaoling Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi he paid homage at the Xiaoling tombs.

sentences.zh: 群臣备法驾，奉寶玺，迎呼萬岁。

translations.literal: The civil and military officials prepared the imperial equipage, presented the imperial seal, and welcomed him with shouts of “ten thousand years.”
translations.idiomatic: The officials arrayed the imperial regalia, bore up the seals, and welcomed him with ten thousand cries of long life.

sentences.zh: 王升辇，詣奉天殿即皇帝位。

translations.literal: The Prince mounted the palanquin, proceeded to the Hall of Imperial Heaven, and there assumed the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: He mounted the palanquin, entered the Hall of Imperial Heaven, and took the throne.

sentences.zh: 复周王橚、齊王榑爵。

translations.literal: He restored the titles of the Prince of Zhou Zhu Su and the Prince of Qi Zhu Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He restored the ranks of the Prince of Zhou, Zhu Su, and the Prince of Qi, Zhu Fu.

sentences.zh: 壬申，葬建文皇帝。

translations.literal: On the renshen day, he buried the Jianwen Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen he buried the Jianwen emperor.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，殺齊泰、黄子澄、方孝孺，並夷其族。

translations.literal: On the dingchou day, he executed Qi Tai, Huang Zicheng, and Fang Xiaoru, and exterminated their clans as well.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou he put Qi Tai, Huang Zicheng, and Fang Xiaoru to death and extirpated their kin to the last degree.

sentences.zh: 坐奸黨死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Those who died on the charge of faction were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Very many died as accomplices of the faction.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，迁興宗孝康皇帝主於陵園，仍稱懿文太子。

translations.literal: On the wuyin day, he moved the tablet of Emperor Xiaokang of Xingzong to the mausoleum precinct and still styled him Crown Prince Yiwen.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin he moved the shrine of Emperor Xiaokang of Xingzong into the imperial cemetery and continued to name him Crown Prince Yiwen.

sentences.zh: 八月壬子，侍讀解缙、編修黄淮入直文淵閣。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the renzi day, Reader-in-Waiting Xie Jin and Compiler Huang Huai entered attendance at the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on renzi, Reader-in-Waiting Xie Jin and Compiler Huang Huai took up duty in the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 尋命侍讀胡广，修撰楊榮，編修楊士奇，檢討金幼孜、故俨同入直，並預機務。

translations.literal: Soon he ordered Reader-in-Waiting Hu Guang, Compiler Yang Rong, Compiler Yang Shiqi, Reviser Jin Youzi, and Hu Yan likewise to enter attendance, all participating in confidential affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also summoned Hu Guang, Yang Rong, Yang Shiqi, Jin Youzi, and Hu Yan to the same inner service, each to share in the highest counsel.

sentences.zh: 執兵部尚書铁铉至，不屈，殺之。

translations.literal: Tie Xuan, Minister of War, was brought in under arrest; he would not submit; he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Tie Xuan, minister of war, was brought in chains. He would not bow. He was executed.

sentences.zh: 左軍都督劉真鎮遼東。

translations.literal: Liu Zhen, Left Commander-in-Chief of the Army, was stationed in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhen, left commander-in-chief, was posted to guard Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，分遣御史察天下利弊。

translations.literal: On the dingsi day, censors were dispatched in separate missions to inspect the benefits and harms throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi he sent censors abroad to survey what helped or hurt the realm.

sentences.zh: 戊午，都督何福為征虏將軍，鎮宁夏，節制陕西行都司。

translations.literal: On the wuwu day, Commander He Fu was made General Who Subdues the Barbarians and stationed in Ningxia, with control over the Shaanxi Regional Military Commission.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Commander He Fu was named General Who Subdues the Barbarians, garrisoned at Ningxia, and given charge of the Shaanxi regional command.

sentences.zh: 都督同知韩观练兵江西，節制广東、福建。

translations.literal: Assistant Commander Han Guan trained troops in Jiangxi and had control over Guangdong and Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Commander Han Guan drilled troops in Jiangxi and held authority over Guangdong and Fujian.

sentences.zh: 甲子，西平侯沐晟鎮云南。

translations.literal: On the jiazi day, the Marquis of Xiping Mu Sheng was stationed in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the Marquis of Xiping, Mu Sheng, took up his post in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 九月甲申，論靖難功，封丘福淇國公，朱能成國公，張武等侯者十三人，徐祥等伯者十一人。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on the jiashen day, rewards for pacifying the difficulty were assessed; Qiu Fu was enfeoffed as Duke of Qi, Zhu Neng as Duke of Cheng, Zhang Wu and others as marquises—thirteen men—and Xu Xiang and others as earls—eleven men.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on jiashen, service in the Pacification was rewarded: Qiu Fu became Duke of Qi, Zhu Neng Duke of Cheng; thirteen men including Zhang Wu were made marquises and eleven including Xu Xiang were made earls.

sentences.zh: 論欸附功，封驸馬都尉王宁為侯，茹瑺、陳瑄及都督同知王佐皆為伯。

translations.literal: Rewards for timely submission were assessed; the Emperor’s Son-in-Law Wang Ning was enfeoffed as marquis; Ru Yao, Chen Xuan, and Assistant Commander Wang Zuo were all made earls.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had come over in time were also honored: the emperor’s son-in-law Wang Ning was made a marquis; Ru Yao, Chen Xuan, and Assistant Commander Wang Zuo were each made an earl.

sentences.zh: 甲午，定功臣死罪减禄例。

translations.literal: On the jiawu day, the precedent was fixed whereby meritorious officials guilty of capital crimes might have their stipends reduced instead.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu he fixed the rule that a meritorious minister condemned to death might instead suffer a cut in stipend.

sentences.zh: 乙未，徙山西民無田者實北平，賜之钞，复五年，韩观為征南將軍，鎮广西。

translations.literal: On the yiwei day, commoners of Shanxi without land were moved to settle in Beiping; they were given paper money; taxes were remitted for five years; Han Guan was made General Who Campaigns South and stationed in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei landless families from Shanxi were resettled in Beiping, paid in paper notes, and granted five years’ tax relief. Han Guan was named General Who Campaigns South and posted to Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丁巳，命北平州縣弃官避靖難兵者朱宁等二百一十九人入粟免死，戍興州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the dingsi day, he ordered that the two hundred nineteen men of Beiping prefectures and counties—including Zhu Ning—who had abandoned office to avoid the Pacification troops should pay grain to escape death and be banished to guard Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In winter’s tenth month, on dingsi, he ruled that two hundred nineteen officials of Beiping—including Zhu Ning—who had fled their posts during the war might buy their lives with grain and go into exile at Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 己未，脩《太祖實錄》。

translations.literal: On the jiwei day, the Veritable Records of Taizu were revised.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei work began on revising the Veritable Records of Taizu.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，鎮远侯顧成鎮貴州。

translations.literal: On the bingyin day, the Marquis of Zhenyuan Gu Cheng was stationed in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the Marquis of Zhenyuan, Gu Cheng, took up his command in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 壬申，徙封谷王橞於长沙。

translations.literal: On the renshen day, the Prince of Gu Zhu Yunyi was transferred in enfeoffment to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen the Prince of Gu, Zhu Yunyi, was moved to a new fief at Changsha.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，詔从征將士掠民間子女者還其家。

translations.literal: On the jiaxu day, an edict ordered that campaign soldiers who had seized commoners’ sons and daughters should return them to their families.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu an edict commanded that any soldier who had taken children from the people during the campaign must send them home.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬辰，立妃徐氏為皇后。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the renchen day, Consort Xu was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renchen, Lady Xu was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 廢广澤王允熥、懷恩王允熞為庶人。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangze Zhu Yunhuang and the Prince of Huai’en Zhu Yunxiao were demoted to commoners.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Guangze, Zhu Yunhuang, and the Prince of Huai’en, Zhu Yunxiao, were stripped to common rank.

sentences.zh: 十二月癸丑，蠲被兵州縣明年夏税。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the guichou day, the summer tax of the next year was remitted for prefectures and counties that had suffered from the armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on guichou, he remitted the next summer’s levy for every district the war had touched.
